items.name: Serdar Akinan
items.title: Düğmeye basıldı. AKP rejimi hızla çöküyor. Gözlerimiz önünde bir devri sabık başladı.
items.transkript: Hello everyone. First of all, you'll  say, "Serdar, why are you wearing your  holiday clothes?" I mean, like a  circumcision boy, you don't normally  wear such colorful things. Honestly,  that smile inside me is starting to  show on the outside. You'll understand  why in a moment. Like everyone else, I  know, more or less, what the tsunami,  whose preliminary waves we've seen,  means. Therefore, like everyone who is  worried about Turkey, about Atatürk's  Turkey, I see very clearly that the end  is inevitable for the AK Party  government, for the Erdoğan regime.  Now, today we will talk about the  operations that have been carried out,  how far this fund scandal has extended,  and what it hasn't. We will especially  examine the images from Serbia and the  victory of the young people. But before  we get to that, yesterday at the  Istanbul Bar Association...the images  that came in are so important that  certain circles who understand this  matter, who know what it means, are in  a state of panic. I'm saying this very  clearly. So, the fact that Ümit  Kocasakal is winning the Istanbul Bar  Association presidency with his team,  and the allegations and statements made  by this team, I think we need to watch  all of this slowly, savoring it. Now, I  mentioned this to you the other day. I  said that I investigated the  prosecutors who filed 25 or 26 lawsuits  against me, almost one every month,  which I know are unjust and unlawful,  for misleading the public, doing this  and that. Because when you log into  UYAP (the Turkish judicial information  system), you can see the name and  surname of the prosecutor who filed the  lawsuit against you. When you Google  their name and surname, their social  media accounts come up. Through their  social media accounts, you can see the  background of those people, those  prosecutors: which schools they came  from, which cities they came from, why  they made visits with AK Party  provincial chairmen and AK Party  municipalities in the places where they  worked. You can see all of this very  clearly. AK Youth speeches and so on.  Now, this event is so important, and  first of all, Ümit Kocasakal's  statement, "It is an uprising," is very  important. I want to show you that  first. Let's all watch it together and  discuss it. >> There is an uprising against the  Republic. I'm saying this openly. The  upcoming period will be one in which,  under the guise of a so-called " terror-free Turkey," a new constitution  will be discussed, and with this  constitution, the unitary structure of  the nation-state, the founding values  and institutions of the Republic will  be sacrificed, or attempts will be made  to sacrifice them, for a so-called  peace. That's what I'm saying. In other  words, a new constitution will be made  with an authority not included in the  constitution. The first four articles  will be changed. The official language  will cease to be solely Turkish. The  definition of citizenship will be  changed. It will be based on an ethnic  foundation. This is a project to create  a mentally and ideologically divided  Turkey. I'm saying it more clearly.  Through a so-called civil and  libertarian new constitution, the 1923  Republic will be abolished and a new  state and regime will be established.  That's the goal. Let me open a  parenthesis. Actually, our  constitutionalists should explain this,  but as you know, according to Article 6  of the Constitution, no person or  institution can exercise a state  authority not derived from the  Constitution. I ask, is there any  provision in the Constitution that  allows the parliament to create a new  constitution? Nowhere. Therefore,  attempting to create a new constitution  through a usurpation of authority and  sovereignty is a clear coup attempt.  And what truly touched my heart was  Professor Korkut Kanadoğlu's speech,  especially its importance, its striking  nature, and its approach that was not  at all condescending, but exactly as it  should be. I especially urge you to  watch it. >> I also want to make a call. Turkey is  being governed by a regime that is  systematically moving towards  authoritarianism, even totalitarianism,  within a system of lawlessness. I am  addressing all judges and prosecutors  serving on the bench. Judges who do not  comply with the decisions of the  Constitutional Court, judges of  criminal courts who issue arbitrary  arrest warrants. We are taking note of  you. >> We are monitoring every decision you  make. We are reporting these decisions.  We will share these with the public,  and we will not sit back and say that  the judiciary is not independent. These  judges and prosecutors should know that  if they think they can disregard the  law, inflict suffering on lawyers and  citizens, and bear no responsibility  for it, they should know that we will  hold them accountable. >> This is such an important stance, such  a clear stance, that it takes a huge  risk. By the way, this professor is the  son of Sabih Kanadoğlu, a well-known  and hated figure among AK Party members . So, they will criticize him a lot.  They will use him as a scapegoat. But  this is the nature of this situation.  And look at what we've experienced  consecutively; don't just see this as  the Istanbul Bar Association. The  initial waves aren't coming only from  Istanbul. Look at the ballot boxes in  different provinces and districts in  recent weeks. For example, the Kocaeli  Chamber of Industry lost 38 to 0, the  Kütahya Chamber of Industry lost 15 to  0, the Dinar Chamber of Industry lost 8  to 1, the Bursa Chamber of Industry  lost 82 to 74, the Istanbul Bar  Association No. 2 lost 102 to 1016, the  Ankara Bar Association No. 2 lost 1006  to 903, and the Ardahan Chamber of  Industry lost members of the AK Party's  Municipal Council. Where does the  reaction come from? From the chambers.  That is, from the bar associations, and  if everyone who has the political  support of the AK Party is directly  targeted, this tells us a lot. Is there  the will to understand this? I don't  think so. Now, those who are running  for office by creating the perception  that they have Erdoğan's support,  those who are still sitting in those  seats and want to protect them, those  who say "Erdoğan is behind me, Ankara  is behind me," are not only targeting  the chamber and bar association  elections. There are other elections as  well. There is another wave coming from  the bottom, at the neighborhood and  district level. This unrest, especially  with this funding crisis, affects 2.5  million families. When you look at the  profile of these 2.5 million families,  Erdoğan goes up to the podium and says , "We have a base that criticizes us.  It's a steel core. Therefore, we listen  carefully. We are doing what is  necessary." He's not actually doing  anything. He's trying to save face as  much as possible. He says, "If there  are 3 million people, let me try to pay  the money for 1 million of them. Let me  put them all in the same category."  However, the suffering he's creating is  growing, deepening, and becoming toxic  over time. And the instruments to  overcome this, the people who will  manage those instruments, the competent  decision-makers, the gatekeepers in  their positions, are crumbling. The  true face of that famous Turkish  century fairy tale, marketed to the  Turkish nation with empty slogans and  glittering commercials, has finally  been revealed. It turns out that  century is not the century of the  nation, not the century of Türkiye. It  was the century of a privileged class,  a privileged group, that left 2.5  million citizens, our compatriots,  under the rubble with an organized  scheme, a stock market manipulation.  Today, the political and moral backbone  of the AK Party has been broken down  the middle. I'm not saying it's cracked , I'm saying it's broken. We are not  just facing a picture of stock market  speculation or an isolated case of  corruption. We are facing one of the  most shameless, brazen, vile,  dishonorable, and plundering mechanisms  in history, built by sitting in the  state's control mechanisms, using  public funds and bureaucratic shields.  And at the very center of this decay is  the palace itself. Look, he served as  the chief advisor to the palace. He sat  in a parliamentary seat for the party.  Moreover, he took on the role of the  theorist of that flashy "Turkish  Century" concept. Ertan Aydın, like  others, was first arrested, then  released, and placed under house arrest . Now, as I'm telling you, a mechanical  process is underway. I see it very  clearly. That's why I'm smiling. That's  why I'm dressed in my best clothes and  appearing before you. They can't figure  out what that mechanism is. That  mechanical state apparatus is biting  here and there. If you notice, lately,  one head of an AKP member has been  rolling one after another. How many  more AKP members will go in the coming  days? How many more will be torn apart  by the lions sitting in that Colosseum  I likened it to, next to Erdoğan,  those wretched souls? Now those sitting  in those boxes are coming. Because he's  started to get rid of the men who built  that whole system. What were you until  yesterday? We'll go wherever it goes.  So what were you, father? Were you the  protector of the small investor? Or a  Trojan horse? I'm saying this very  clearly. Are you a Trojan horse hiding  in this scam, or are you the protector  of the small investor? On January 13,  2025, Ertan Aydın is appointed as an  independent board member of Tera  Yatırım Menkul Değerler. Now, what  is the equivalent of that seat? What is  his role? The company is supposed to  protect the meager savings of small  investors, retirees, and civil servants  against the controlling shareholders.  So what happened? Tera's public  offering of Vişne Madencilik (a  Turkish mining company) was worth 37.4  lira in February 2025, but it was  recovered by Tera's portfolio's special  fund for privileged groups–and I  emphasize, for privileged groups. By  July 2025, it had increased 23 times  its value, reaching 859 lira. Then  Ertan Aydın took office, and the  bubble was inflated. It reached its  peak in an instant. On June 23, 2025,  Ertan Aydın was the first jackal to  jump ship, admitting it himself: "I saw  some problems and consulted with our  senior figures before leaving." Could  those senior figures be Erdoğan? Now  we ask: When you saw those problems,  did you run to the Capital Markets  Board (SPK)? What did you do? Instead  of doing that, instead of going to the  prosecutors, instead of going to the  Capital Markets Board (SPK), which you  had the power to do, instead of doing  what you could have done with a single  phone call at the time, you didn't do  it. You collected your money and ran  away. After you, Tera shares plummeted.  The shares crashed by 90%, leaving  hundreds of thousands of families  devastated and crying out in anguish.  For months, no one touched this man. No  one could touch these men, these people . Because everyone knew this: "Is  Erdoğan behind this? Is this  protective shield, this hidden shield,  really Erdoğan?" And you've set up a  revolving door system here. You're  getting licenses. Public funds,  nepotism, and this robbery cannot be  explained by the audacity of an  individual bureaucrat or a ruthless  brokerage firm. You can't explain it. " Wow, they're so audacious. What kind of  people are they? What does this have to  do with anything? It's a three-legged  mechanism institutionalized at the top  of the state. It's very clear to see  that apparatus, that mechanism. There's  the regulation and licensing aspect."  Who gave Tera Investment Bank its  establishment and operating license in  the corridors of the Banking Regulation  and Supervision Agency (BDDK)? Who gave  it? I'm asking. The BDDK administration  at the time injected public funds. From  the BDDK to the Central Bank, from  there to Türkiye Sigorta, Türkiye  Hayat Emeklilik, and those who were  placed at the very top of those  positions. Now, who owns these? The  Sovereign Wealth Fund. Erdoğan himself . Who channeled citizens 'savings,  public deposits, into these dubious  funds in exchange for millions of  dollars of personal gain? On one side  of the table sits the regulator. On the  other side sits the actors who siphoned  off public funds. Sometimes they wear  the same robe, the same jacket. Sons,  sons-in-law, and the sons of former  ministers and presidents who have  immunity, the sons-in-law of deputy  ministers, key companies, key  managements, firms that are given  privileges, injected with money, and  given intelligence. This whole system,  you're all unaware of each other,  especially Erdoğan, is a multi-billion  dollar system. Did someone say, "Don't  touch this scheme, the state is behind  it. The power of politics is behind it.  They'll destroy you"? Those prosecutors , that Capital Markets Board, that  Banking Regulation and Supervision  Agency, they all thought, "Erdoğan  will destroy us. We can't get out from  under this wreckage." But if you notice , Erdoğan can't get out from under  that wreckage now. The AK Party can't  get out. The secret to the AK Party's  collapse lies precisely here. Every  time Erdoğan gets into the microphone,  he talks about the interest rate lobby,  foreign powers, morality, and "I came  with a ring." He says some people want  to get rich unjustly. And so on. Your  chief advisor has taken millions from  the people. We still don't know where  your former minister, Fatma Betül  Sayankaya, got 130 million. Millions  are circulating. And the people are  saying, "When am I going to get my  money back?" I said suicides would  happen. Companies are going bankrupt.  There will be mass layoffs next month.  It will definitely happen. And people  who have nothing to do with these jobs,  who are just ordinary people, will  suddenly find themselves standing at  their door, unable to pay rent, unable  to pay their child's tuition, unable to  go to the hospital. Do you think those  responsible for this will remain in  their positions? Now I ask you, a very  simple question: How did the mechanisms  coordinated by the Turkish Sovereign  Wealth Fund and the Treasury approve  the transfer of the people's insurance  and pension savings to this fund? Did  you knowingly turn a blind eye, or were  you powerless? Just before the bubble  burst, according to MASAK and stock  exchange data, which political elites  and bureaucratic relatives realized  their profits and fled the market?  Ertan Aydın says he consulted with our  elders. Who are these elders? Who are  they? Explain it. Are you falling for  this scheme? How did they know all this  and remain silent? How did they know  all this and not go to the Capital  Markets Board, to the prosecutors? Get  lost. Your bombastic tales. 2.5 million  people are victims. Oh, I hear the  anguish from here. Thousands of  kilometers away, your accomplices are  saying, "We'll handle this." The  gentleman is furious, very angry. He'll  take this, he'll take that. But the  gentleman isn't doing anything. While  those prosecutors in Türkiye whose  names you don't know are acting as dogs , those whose names we don't know are  carrying out these operations. That's  why I say you're only seeing the  credits of the film. You can't get out  of this swamp. Look, I'm being very  clear. We know their names. All their  names are on record. Today, these names  we're talking about are being taken by  the neck, placed under house arrest,  then a warrant for arrest is issued.  Then prison. Who? A member of  parliament. Which party? The AK Party.  What did they do before? They were part  of Erdoğan's inner circle. What did  they do? They came up with the slogan " Turkey's Century." Look at this! The  guy is going to prison. Look, if those  who signed the permits for this scheme,  those who transferred funds, those who  leaked information from inside and  filled their coffers–if these people  aren't held accountable, we, I'm saying  this very clearly, cannot hold the AK  Party accountable, we cannot get them  to account for their actions. As the  spine collapses, we will find all the  nerve endings connected to it. We  already have documents and information.  And let me tell you, that's why I'm  speaking with a smile now. The  undercurrent is growing. I see it very  clearly. Ankara is boiling. There's no  escaping it, gentlemen, ladies, there's  no escaping it. I want to tell you  about the Serbian elections, which I  think are very striking. The images you  see >> came from Serbia last night. It's such  an interesting story that I want you to  listen carefully. What did the youth  achieve in Serbia? Look, it's such a  similar story that behind this victory  in Serbia are two cities. One is Novi  Pazar, in northern Serbia, a major city , a center of culture and education.  50,000 students live there. Now look at  another city. Novi Pazar, in the south,  a poor and deliberately neglected city  where Bosniak Muslims are the majority.  The pain of war and massacres, the  Bosnian War, is still being felt there.  For two years, these two cities have  been racing towards the same goal with  a single wind. What is it? The student  movement. Do you know how these events  started? Two years ago, in Novi Sad, a  train station was being renovated with  Chinese funding and support. The  station had a concrete canopy. The  canopy collapsed. Sixteen people died.  What happened? It's very simple. A  symbol of corruption, nepotism, and  lack of oversight. Sounds familiar,  doesn't it? I think so too. Now  students are coming forward. They say,  "Brother, we want the tender processes  that ended the lives of these 16 people , all these documents, to be revealed  and accountability demanded." So what  are the government, the pro-government  structures, the media doing? Prime  Minister Vučević says contemptuously,  "Who are you?" You should ask that.  Suddenly, the demonstrations reach  100,000 people. The mayor of Novi Sad  and the prime minister resign, but the  protests continue. And Alexander  Vučević, a dog in politics since 1993 , was the information minister and  responsible for censorship during the  Milošević era. A cesspool of filth.  Since 2014, he's been either prime  minister or president, taking over and  over again, running the market. He  controls the media. According to him,  the opposition is a Western agent.  Sounds familiar, doesn't it? What's his  biggest trump card? Foreign policy. He  says, "I have very good relations with  the EU, Russia, China, America, and  Turkey. That's why I don't face  pressure from outside." Again, sounds  familiar, doesn't it? And to open up  his mandate, he resigns from the  presidency and runs for prime minister.  Now, this is where things get crucial.  Young people are starting boycotts in  universities, and forums are being  established. I think this is a sign of  democratic politics. We say that  fascism is rising not just in Türkiye,  but in every country in the world. The  images coming from Brazil are extremely  promising, I think, brother. They are  doing something very important. There  is no single leader here. That's very  important. Decisions are made through  consensus, and if necessary, by voting,  and rectors and academics–the  academic community–stand by the  students. Most importantly, Bosnian and  Serbian youth are walking this path  together. They say, "We will do  something that puts aside our old  problems. Our problem is not identity  politics." While walking along the road , a monastery offers halal breakfast to  these young Bosnian people, and do you  know what these students are doing in a  process of forming a political party?  They say, "We don't trust the current  opposition. We collect 10,000  signatures." With 10,000 signatures,  they create an electoral list of 250  people. They say, "We are creating an  alternative." The vast majority of  opposition parties withdraw from the  race in favor of these students. What  happens? The list effectively becomes  the main opposition. Now, what are the  candidacy criteria? Not being a student , not being a high-ranking opposition  or ruling party member, and having a  clean record. It's quite simple. During  the election process, the  representatives are distributed  proportionally to university cities and  faculties. Candidates are determined in  these forums. 99 candidates are  challenged. 38 are removed from the  list. Even the Rector of Belgrade  University is vetoed for denying the  Srebrenica massacre, and the profile of  the list is half academics, 60%have  PhDs, are urban, and predominantly  upper-middle class. And who is the  first-ranked candidate? Lilya  Sradanovic, a cardiology professor. The  sixth-ranked candidate is very  interesting. He's a Bosnian Muslim who  studied and graduated from Sakarya  University, and speaks Turkish. Adem  Mavrić, the representative of Novi  Pazar. It's a very nice story. And they  say: We have 11 fundamental promises:  Judicial independence, purging corrupt  public officials, transparency in  tenders, media freedom, meritocracy in  public service, education reform,  support for entrepreneurship, better  working conditions, dismantling of  monopolies, social housing, healthcare  in rural areas, and maintaining a  balance between the West, Russia, and  China in foreign policy. We will react  to the genocide in Gaza and we support  sanctions against Israel. A poem. A  poem. An 11-point poem. And what  happened, man? They declared victory.  Today, in the streets of Serbia, songs  of independence and victory are being  sung. What can we say? May it happen to  us too. I've been saying this from the  beginning. Yes. So, Ümit Kocasakal's  victory in the Istanbul Bar Association , you could call it the victory of the  nationalists, you could call it the  victory of Atatürk's Turkey. Whatever  happens, we will not allow anyone to  tamper with the fundamental values of  the Republic of Turkey. This Kurdish  issue, this opening, this and that...We  won't fall for these tricks anymore,  enough is enough, "he said, and used  the phrase" an uprising against the  Republic. "I draw your attention to  this. He used the expression," You are  in the midst of an uprising against the  Republic. "This is a spark. What should  follow this spark, I insist, is never  the established political system. What  should happen is that young people,  perhaps like in Serbia, organize  themselves, sit down at the table with  the opposition, and say," Brother, you  step aside. We are coming with a brand  new list. "I claim, I assert, that the  biggest party in Türkiye will be the  Undecided Party. Not nationalist  parties, not whatever other parties.  The citizens are waiting for this. Look , 11 points. They put forward 11 points , and these guys won. The young people  won. It's a very good model. It's a  very good model. I attach great  importance to it being a leaderless  movement. This is a practice. Did they  win in practice? Yes, they did. Is  there hope? There is still hope. That's  why I smile and always say it: You  can't prosper through oppression. The  oppression Erdoğan is perpetrating,  the system he's established, is a  gang-like structure with nothing to do  with politics. It's a gang. And today,  look, the Azerbaijani president, that  same gang, got into a discussion about  whose head is bigger, excuse me. Aliyev  said," You'll take this head. "Can you  imagine? The headscarf issue is their  most sensitive issue. His chief advisor , a friend of many years, betrayed him  in two seconds. He told him to pack up  his office and leave. Pack up his  office and leave. Because Aliyev has  work to do, man. He has work to do.  Erdoğan is that kind of man. He took  the head. Come on, Islamists, speak up!  Aliyev is coming to Ankara now. Aliyev  is coming to Ankara. He's imposed a  headscarf ban right next to you. Muslim  girls, young girls can't go to school  with headscarves. Yes, sir. In short,  that's the agenda. And that's what I  see every day, with more enjoyable,  more beautiful news. Well, our hearts  ache, let them ache. Well, we have a  lot of damage, so be it. Well, we are a  nation that fought a war of  independence. We founded this country,  singing the song of sovereignty under  much worse conditions. We will not  leave this country to three jackals,  three packs of dogs who use Islam and  God to get rich. The songs sung  yesterday, this photograph, this image  rising from Istanbul yesterday, will  come from all over Türkiye tomorrow.  Have no doubt. The heads of those who  don't deserve it will roll. I'm sure  they're asking," Who did this? "It  doesn't matter who did it. This is a  will. That will has begun to manifest  itself. So don't lose hope. I've always  said, don't lose hope. That's all I'm  saying. Have a good day everyone.

items.title: MURAT AĞIREL, GÖKÇEK ÖRGÜTÜ ÜYESİ Mİ? | KARGA KAHVALTISINI YAPMADAN | 27 EKİM SALI | TİMUR SOYKAN
items.transkript: Günaydın. Günaydın güzelim memleketin güzel insanları. Karga kahvaltısını yapmadan hoş geldiniz. Bugün 27 Ekim Salı ve gündemimiz yine çok dolu. Hızlıca başlıyoruz. Birincisi Cumhurbaşkanı Erdoğan kabine toplantısının ardından açıklamalar yaptı. Şoke edici açıklamalardı. Açıkçası beni şoke etti. Açıklama şöyle: "Bizim ne basın özgürlüğüyle ne de eleştirel seslerle bir sorunumuz vardır." Ya hiç sorunumuz yok dedi basın özgürlüğüyle. Eleştirilerle de sorunumuz yok dedi. "Türkiye medya çeşitliliği açısından dünyanın en ileri ülkelerinden biridir." Yani siz telefon televizyon kumandasını elinize alıyorsunuz ve Erdoğan konuşurken kanalları geziyorsunuz. Her yerde aynı ekranı görüyorsunuz ya. Bu bir çeşit çeşitlilikmiş. Ve örneğin Halk TV'ye geldiğinizde tak ah bakıyorsunuz yayın yok. Tele1'e geliyorsunuz simsiyah ekran ama çeşitlilik varmış. Yani ülkenin %95'ini biliyorsunuz medyası eee yani iktidar kontrolünde ama Erdoğan'a göre öyle değilmiş. "Avrupa'da televizyon kanalı sayısı itibarıyla ülkemiz ilk sıralarda yer alıyor." Evet televizyon sayısı fazla olabilir ama aynı ekranlar aynı yayınlar yani fark etmiyor. Ya kumandayla değiştirseniz de aynı yayınlar olduğu için çok fazla sayıda olması bir anlam ifade etmiyor. "Her görüşten Bakın burası önemli. Her görüşten yüzlerce televizyon kanalı, binlerce radyo kanalı ülkemizde özgürce yayın yapıyor." Halk TV'nin önünde geçen biliyorsunuz polis barikatları vardı. Uğur Mumcu'nun duvarda resimleri olduğu televizyon binasına polisler girdi ve yayını kestiler. Aynı şekilde Tele1, Merdan Yanardağ'ın yani kanalın kurucusu Merdan Yanardağ'ın ifadesi bile alınmadan kayyum tarafından ele geçirildi. Sanırım kayyumun yönettiği şu an 20 tane televizyon kanalı var. Her görüşten yüzlerce televizyon kanalı var derken Erdoğan neyi kastetti? Gerçekten bilmiyoruz. Ve şöyle devam ediyor. Biz de bunu Türkiye'nin sosyolojik çeşitliliğinin bir sembolü o sembolü olarak görüyor, farklı sesleri memnuniyetle karşılıyoruz. Yani Halk TV niye kapalı diye sorabilirsiniz tabii veya Tele1 niye kapalı diye. Örneğin TV24 niye kapatıldı? İşte yaklaşık bu fon skandalı, fon vurgunu yani Asrın Vurgunu sırasında 2000'e yakın sanırım sosyal medya hesabı engellendi. Onlarca gazeteci cezaevinde ama Erdoğan bunları söyledi. Ben kesinlikle Erdoğan'ın yaşadığı ülkede yaşamak istiyorum. Yani Erdoğan'ın tarif ettiği bir gazeteci olarak Erdoğan'ın tarif ettiği bu ülkede yaşamak istiyorum. Ama o ülke neresi acaba? Bulamıyorum. Ama Türkiye'nin o ülke olmadığına eminim. Çünkü bir de şunu düşünmenizi istiyorum. Erdoğan bu sözleri söylüyor ve siz cezaevindeki bir gazetecisiniz. Yani dört duvar arasındasınız. Belki yalnız tecrit koşullarındasınız. Belki İsmail Arı gibi 23 kişilik koğuşta 63 kişiyle yaşıyorsunuz. Bir de o orayı var etmiş, orayı kurmuş insanların üzerine bu yükü bırakıyorsunuz yani. Yok ediyorsunuz yani. Ama Erdoğan ne dedi? Şey, her görüşten yüzlerce televizyon kanalı, binlerce radyo kanalı ülkemizde özgürce yayın yapıyor. Merdan abi cezaevinde izlerken ne hissetmiştir? Necati Özkan cezaevinde izlerken ne hissetmiştir değil mi? O saçma sapan casusluk davasında. Ve diyor ki yani bu kadar akıl dışı, mantık dışı bir iddianameyle biz nasıl hapsediliyoruz diyor. Son gelişmeleri veriyorum bir de kim rahat bu ülkede? Erdoğan'ın dediği özgürlükleri kimler yaşıyor? İsmailağa cemaatinin mensubu var, Muhammed Serkan Gül. Onun böyle Mahmut Efendi biliyorsunuz o tarikatın lideri. Onun dine davet binasını ziyaret etmiş. Bakın onlar da sosyal medyada bu kişi sosyal medyada takip ediliyor, şey yapılıyor cemaatten. Onun video görüntüleri var. Böyle geliyor. Böyle de video kaydediyorlar. Böyle lüksün sonu yok. Yani bir hırka bir lokma bir hayat değil yani. Ultra lüks hayatlar. Mahmut Efendi'nin şeyine bakın. Mahmut Efendi deyince Mahmut hatırladınız mı? Sel felaketinde hayatını kaybetti. İsmailağa cemaatine Fatih'te verilen otopark vardı usulsüz, yasa dışı bir şekilde. O otoparkın önündeki elektrik altyapısını bile yapmışlardı. Araba geçe geçe yıpratmışlardı. Bu Mahmut Usta, Mahmut Oğlunun dan adını alan o yapıya cemaate mensup olan 14 yaşındaki Mahmut ayakkabıları ıslanmasın diye eline almıştı ve yalın ayak oradan geçerken elektrik çarpmış, sonucu ölüm ölüm. Şimdi burada görüntüler nasıl? Ultra lüks arabalar. Mahmut öldü. Bakın bir görüntü daha verelim. Tarikatlar diyorum ya her zaman altın dönemlerini yaşıyorlar. Onlar özgür. Burası da Menzil. Bursa'da temel atma töreni. Külliye yapıyorlar devasa Serhendi grubu. Bunlar biliyorsunuz bölündüler. Birbirlerini kardeş üç kardeş ayrı ayrı artık Menzil'de yapıyorlar ve birbirlerini eee vakfın paralarını yani tarikatın müritlerinden toplanan paraları çalmakla suçluyorlar. Kimse onlara dokunmuyor. Yani 50 milyarlık bir varlıkları var paylaşamadıkları. Daha neler neler var? Binalar falan. Hepsi birbirine diyor ki bak müritlerden aldık biz bu paraları müritlerden topladık sonra da üstlerine geçirdi diyorlar. Yani bir çeşit yolsuzluk, devasa bir yolsuzluk ihbarı. Onlara da kimse dokunmuyor. Onlar çok özgür. Onların televizyon kanalları da özgür, her şey özgür. Bak burada temel atma törenine geliyor. Bunlar Serhendi grubu. Kardeşlerden en büyüğü bu. Onlara devam ediyorlar. Bakın burada bir de bir haber daha var. Söylemezsem kötü hissedeceğim kendimi gerçekten. Ben Fethullahçılarla çok mücadele ettik. Fethullahçılar arkadaşlarımızı hapse attı. Çok uzun süre yani onların karanlık faaliyetlerine tepki gösterdik. AKP ile ortak hareket ediyorlardı. Kumpas kurdular, arkadaşlarımızı cezaevine attılar, bizi tehditler ettiler. Gazetecileri işsiz bıraktılar. Bu ülkenin bu anti-demokratik sürecinde çok büyük katkı şeyleri var. Sonuçları var yani bunu birlikte yaptılar. Ama bir 73 yaşındaki Abdullah Tırpan varmış. 55 yıllık esnafmış Tekirdağ'da. FETÖ üyeliğinden 7 yıl 6 ay hapis cezası almış. Ve bu kişi diyabet hastası olduğu için bacağı kangren olmuş ve kesilmiş. Tahliye çağrıları yapılmış, karşılıksız kalmış. Ve Mustafa Yeneroğlu da yazmış Serbest Diyette bunu. Cezaevinde abi ölüm haberi gelirse bu soruyu sormuş olan herkesin bir ölümde payı olmayacak mı diye. Kızı da geçen hafta çağrı yapmış sosyal medya hesabında. Abdullah Tırpan cezaevinde öldü. Yani suçlama ne olursa olsun, ne şey olursa olsun, bir insan sağlık, insanların hakları var. İnsanların hakları var. Eee, yarın görüşmek üzere.

items.transkript: You cannot intimidate the youth, the  journalists, or the people who believe  in the bright future of this country.  You cannot make them back down. They >> need to know that they cannot  discourage us like this. At least,  perhaps they would learn if they asked  their old friends. The five people who  disagree will continue to explain  things to those who disagree at this  table. Time sometimes flies like a bird , and sometimes crawls like a worm. But  a person feels best when they don't  notice whether time is passing slowly  or quickly. The quote we took from  Turgenev's "Fathers and Sons" has a  direct connection to the most important  topic of our program. Because this  weekend, Turkey talked about a story of  fathers and sons. But that story of  fathers and sons was perhaps a summary  of the whole background issue. You will  understand why we started with fathers  and sons in a moment. I wish them a  good evening. Welcome, Timur. Thank you . >> Thank you. >> Two of us are greeting you today. First , let me tell you why. Our friends  haven't left us. Don't worry. You know  Murat. Murat is in prison. He continues  to work and struggle in prison. For a  while now, Barış Pehlivan hasn't been  able to see his daughter due to the  circumstances we've been through. He's  seeing his daughter now. Can we call  this good news at the last minute? Yes,  we can call it good news. It's sudden  news. He was >> worried. She became an aunt. That's why  she's not with us. We're both opposite  each other on the program today. >> Yes. Our friend Aslı gave birth. Aslı  is a very old friend of mine. I love  her very much. Aslı and Kenan. Their  baby was born. We have a baby boy. Ali  Kenan. He's a very beautiful baby. I  saw his photos. We wish Aslı and Kenan  happiness. May Ali Kenan have a very  beautiful life. May he have a wonderful , free life. Those are our wishes. >> Now, there's the  Fenerbahçe-Galatasaray match on the  program today. Yes. There's >> a group of guys who want the program to  go by quickly. Don't worry, we have a  lot to talk about. It will be a very  full program, but we'll tell everything  very quickly. You won't even realize  how time flies. You'll say, "The trio  is like a bird." But first, news from  Murat. As you know, Murat was  transferred this week to Kandra prison  in Kocaeli. I want to start by giving  his mailing address. Because Murat is  actually waiting for your letters. Can  we give it to him, friends? Let's start  by giving his mailing address, friends,  because a person in prison has no  communication with the outside world.  You know there's no communication. A  letter is like a morale boost for him.  You ask what we can do, right? You can  write letters. You can make Murat feel  that he's not alone. By the way, I know  many letters are already being written  there. I'm receiving them too. I'll  repeat the mailing address once more:  Kocaeli No. 2 F-type prison, B2 Tire 4,  Tre 61, PTT prison branch. When you  write this much, it will go to the  prison. Of course, it will be read.  Remember, it will be read. >> Don't think only Murat will read it. It >> will be stamped "seen" >> because it will be stamped there.  Unfortunately, prison letters don't  stay between two people. I mean, don't  misunderstand why I'm saying this.  Sometimes they write such things in  prison letters that there are people in  this country who are prosecuted for  writing prison letters because they  went too far. So I say, be careful.  Secondly, Murat sent a letter to our  program. If you want, we can read  Murat's message. I can read it if you  want. >> I would be very happy. >> Hello. Hello, our friends who follow  Onlar TV. Hello, my dear friends. On my  way to becoming Evliya Çelebi, the  authorities have deemed Kocaeli No. 2  F-type prison a suitable stop for me.  For now, I am here. I am alone in a  three-person cell. You know that joke,  "Silivri is cold"? Whoever said that  hasn't seen Kocaeli prison. The  radiators aren't working either, we'll  fix that. Unfortunately, I have neither  a television nor can I read newspapers.  They haven't done my canteen shopping  yet. Problems that would normally be  solved in 5-10 minutes turn into a  Gordian knot when it comes to me. I  don't have unlined A4 paper. It's  forbidden. My heart is pounding because  my pen is about to run out. The prison  administration doesn't allow anyone to  bring pens from outside. It's sold in  the canteen. I previously suffered  tissue loss in my fingers because of  the pens sold there. It improved  somewhat with physical therapy, but  there's still a trace of the 'e' mark  on my finger. Because I write a lot. I  almost use two pens a day. I only have  one pen left now. I haven't been able  to buy anything from the canteen yet. I  haven't been able to see my wife, my  daughter, my son, or my parents. They  didn't even give me phone access.  Because of the cruelty of the financial  police, I couldn't even see my  beautiful daughter, who was waiting in  front of the courthouse. They didn't  let me see her. It's not just me; they  treat everyone like this. Even if the  crime hasn't been proven, young police  officers, only 25 or 30 years old,  don't hesitate to display their  humiliating and heartless behavior. Of  course, I don't mean everyone, but  unfortunately, that's how it is. Isn't  this the first message Murat sent to  our program this Monday? This way...in  Türkiye, even if someone is guilty,  I've witnessed people being treated so  badly in prisons. We have a worldview  that advocates for everyone to be  treated humanely, even if they are  guilty. Therefore, we want treatment  that is in accordance with human rights  and freedoms, not just for Murat, but  for everyone. This is not a favor, not  a luxury. This is a constitutional  obligation, a situation in accordance  with the law. On the other hand, it is  also a historical achievement. >> Exactly. And think about it, Murat Arel  is in prison because he wrote, because  he wrote news, or even because he  didn't write news, and he is worried  about his pen running out. And that pen  is very important to Murat. You know he  is very interested in pens. He is  experiencing distress because he  damages his fingers with that pen. He  also experienced the fear of his pen  running out. A journalist is being  dragged into these conditions. By the  way, we should also add İsmail Arı.  İsmail Arı is staying in a cell  designed for 28 people with 63 people.  He sleeps on the floor in Sincan Prison . Many journalists experience these  serious problems. But today you are  writing a very important news story  about Murat, actually about Murat's  investigation. >> There is a last-minute development. We  will give you some news. Breaking news ...uh, very critical, the kind that  makes you wonder what's happening. And  again, we'll come back to the Tele1  issue, for example, but first, fathers  and sons, you >> continue from there. >> Because the main issue in Türkiye is  the fund issue. >> Uh huh. >> We will continue to do journalism as  always. I think the public's agenda is  our agenda. The most important issue in  Türkiye is the fund issue. Now, this  weekend, Mehmet Ali Akben, the former  head of the Banking Regulation and  Supervision Agency (BDDK), then the  chairman of the board of directors of  Vakıf Katılım, right? Uh huh. >> We talked about fathers and sons  through Mehmet's son, Çakmak Çakmak,  who is at the head of Türkiye Sigorta, >> but this has become too much of a  fathers and sons story. Can you give us  a picture of fathers and sons, F? >> Exactly. We even prepared a graph, a  table of it. Uh, Terkoğlu. But we can  say this, friends, until we put the  table on screen. This actually shows  the point reached in bureaucracy. So,  this fund scandal, which we call the  biggest scandal in the history of the  Republic of Turkey and which will go  down in world history, also reveals the  situation that arose in Türkiye after  the transition to a presidential system . We can say this very honestly. They  say, "There is a bureaucracy. We will  get rid of the bureaucracy. We will  switch to a presidential system. You  will give the authority, and you will  see the effect. It will be much faster, " they said. On the contrary, we see  the formation of a bureaucratic  oligarchy. Initially, I thought that a  one-man regime was the goal, and that  the absence of checks and balances in a  one-man regime would cause major  problems. Now I am absolutely certain  of this. Those who aimed for a one-man  regime in Türkiye have created a  system with many, many people, a  complex hierarchy where there is no  hierarchy. Now, I will stand up for  this, my friends, if my director allows , we are actually seeing this here.  This bureaucratic oligarchy is actually  a picture of a system where checks and  balances have been eliminated, where  everyone can do anything through family  connections, and can do anything.  Because how do we describe the fund  scandal? Normally, a stock gaining  16,000%in value, a massive increase in  value, is something that would never  happen in the world. It's like when an  invention is made, a company patents it , and that's it–for example, they've  found a cure for cancer, or something  like that. The stocks were inflated to  skyrocket like that. This isn't  something that can happen in the world.  They inflated these stocks for a  windfall. So, when I say this is the  summary of the presidential system,  this is it. This is actually the  picture that summarizes it. Now,  normally, what would you say, Barış?  When something like this happens, a  stock that's just a factory, a wall, no  production, not even two cows, a food  company with two employees, could it be  more valuable than Arçelik? Would you  believe that? Normally you wouldn't,  right? But people thought it was  possible under the presidential system.  That's how they fell into this trap. Or  would you consider building an  apartment building next to the Maiden's  Tower? Everyone would say you couldn't.  Or building an apartment building on  the Bosphorus, or the skyscraper on the  Bosphorus. Normally, would you think, " I'm going to build this building on the  edge of the Bosphorus"? You couldn't.  In Europe, or in a country with  democracy, or with robust checks and  balances, you'd say, "Is such a thing  even possible? You wouldn't even dream  of doing that." But these father and  sons have dreamt it. I mean, if we said  we were going to build a skyscraper on  the Bosphorus, next to the Maiden's  Tower, it wouldn't work, would it? How  would that be possible? You'd say it's  impossible. But these people allegedly  said, "We'll increase a stock price by  16,000%and make a fortune from that."  That's the claim. That's the fund  scandal. Now, which father and sons are  involved here? Let's start exactly  where you said. Let's start with the  latest development. The first father  here is Mehmet Ali Akbent. Now, Mehmet  Ali Akbent and his son, Mehmet Emir  Akbent. Now, look, there's a path from  father to son, right? >> A path from father to son. Now,  according to this claim—and I  emphasize claims—we see how the  system works. At >> the heart of it all is Tera. Friends,  at the heart of this is Türkiye  Sigorta AŞ, which belongs to the  Turkish Sovereign Wealth Fund, which  belongs to all of us, that is, to the  public, and here we have the BDDK ( Banking Regulation and Supervision  Agency). Here we have the SPK (Capital  Markets Board). They are all here. In  this whole journey, this connection  from father to son, we will see how the  scandal unfolds. Mehmet Ali Akben is  the former head of the BDDK, the head  of the Banking Regulation and  Supervision Board. What does this board  do? It supervises private financial  institutions, some of the companies you  see here, right? Terabank, for example,  or Tera Holding, private financial  institutions and banks, and it  determines whether they will be granted  licenses, whether their activities will  be suspended, or whether they will be  fined. In essence, it's the highest  supervisory body for the entire  financial and banking system. Now, in  2021, Mehmet Ali Akben is at its head.  And what is his son doing at that time?  Coincidentally, his son is also an  independent board member of a holding  company that is also an agricultural  company called Green Türk. What a  coincidence! Because he is also a board  member of a company whose shares are  traded on the stock exchange and  included in funds. Now you might say, " The father is the former head of the  Banking Regulation and Supervision  Agency (BDDK), and his son is on the  board of directors of a company." He  was born in 1994, I believe, and  graduated from the law faculty of  Medipol University. Generally, that's  how it is with these types. They're  graduates from the law faculties or  various faculties of universities  established during the AKP era. A  complete AKP bureaucrat and his son.  They had a "golden generation" goal,  and now a new generation is emerging.  That's exactly the picture you see when  you look at it. Now you might ask, "How  do Ahmet Emir Akben and Mehmet Ali  Akben's paths intersect?" They  intersect right in the middle, through  Ta Çakmak. Do you know what Ta Çakmak  is doing? Ta Çakmak says, "Buy the  shares of Green Türk for Tera Holding. " Now, what was Ta Çakmak doing?  There's money in the insurance company.  State money. Public money. An insurance  company, and people are getting insured  there. They're giving bonuses, and with  that money, >> you can explain it on camera, right? >> Now, with those things going on, I mean , while Ta Çakmak was at Türkiye  Sigorta AŞ, the claim is that he said  to Terabank, "You should buy the shares  of the company where Ahmet Emir Akben,  the Greek, is on the board of directors ." Terabank said this, and Terabank  invested the money that Türkiye  Sigorta AŞ had in the fund into the  fund to buy these shares. That's the  claim. So, he went and invested this  money in the fund. In return, he asked  them to increase the value of Green  Türk shares, and Tera increased those  shares. So, according to the claim,  what did Ta Çakmak get instead of a  bribe? Instead of a bribe, because he  had Green Türk shares in his  possession and a partnership structure  with them, he achieved something in a  way. With those shares, he already  added value to his company. He earned  very serious money. On the other hand,  he also made Ahmet Emir Ak, the son of  Mehmet Ali Akbey, more valuable in his  holding company. He enabled them to  make money as well. And that wasn't  enough, look. Ta Çakmak received a $ 1  million bribe from Terabank to provide  funds, essentially giving Terabank our  money from the sovereign wealth fund.  The allegations stem from claims that  the private secretaries of the company,  specifically those at Türkiye Sigorta  AŞD (Turkish Insurance Corporation),  were essentially bag carriers. These  individuals are reportedly under arrest , and there are claims of confessions  to this. After describing this  situation, we need to add this: Where  does the "father"(referring to a  powerful figure in the government) come  into play? Why did Terabank provide  them with this advantage? There's a  very clear answer. Because Tera Fund,  or Terolding, wanted to establish a  bank, and to do so, they needed  permission from the BDDK (Banking  Regulation and Supervision Agency).  Mehmet Ali Akben was at the head of the  BDDK in 2021, and he granted Tera  permission to establish a bank. However , in those years, there are records in  the indictments indicating that Kasım  Garipoğlu's illegal dealership money,  amounting to $ 350 million, was  distributed in bags and went to  Terabank. So, Terabank shouldn't  actually be given a license. Because  even if you have a blemish on your  record, even if an intelligence  operation is negative, even if your  name is just on the file, you can't  establish a bank. But this system,  where everyone wins, where the father  and the son, Green Türk, all profit,  and most importantly, where Ta Çakmak  uses the money of a company in  Türkiye's sovereign wealth fund,  ultimately everyone wins. They're all  rolling in money. The shares are  soaring, and there's money and bribery  involved. Now look at this bribery  scheme; Ta Çakmak isn't just taking $  1 million in cash. It's also known that  he earned at least 70-80 million TL  thanks to the fund when he inflated  Green Türk's shares. Because he went  and invested money in the TMSF fund,  which is called the repentance fund. So  we know he made money from there too.  And in this scheme, the complete  outline of the embezzlement and bribery  is revealed. Now imagine that Fatma  Betül Sayankaya is in place of Ta  Çakmak. Fatma Betü Sayankaya  similarly acquired Özata Diricilik  shares, sold them to Teraya, and  profited. This transaction raises a  legitimate question, a justified  question: Did Fatma Betü Sayankaya,  like in the case of Taak, actually  receive that 2.2 billion TL as a bribe?  I think this is a very important  question. Now we move on to another  father-son relationship. I'll explain  it quickly. Mustafa Balcı. Mustafa  Balcı and his son, İskender Balcı.  Mustafa Balcı and İskender Balcı are  again fathers and sons in the finance  sector. Mustafa Balcı is a former  member of the BDDK (Banking Regulation  and Supervision Agency). According to  some claims, he is currently still a  member of the Ethics Committee. So,  their paths intersect again at the BDDK . Mehmet Ali Akben and Mustafa Balcı  worked at the same institution during  the same period. Look, the fathers know  each other. And when we come to the son , İskender Balcı, his connections in  the finance sector aren't just due to  his father. He also has a father-in-law , Osman Çelik, who was the Deputy  Minister of Treasury and Finance. He  resigned. So, he's got connections  through both his father and his  father-in-law. And where did we see  İskender Balcı? Look, Tera again.  Tera everywhere. Because that's where  they're focusing. And what is he doing?  İsmail Balcı is also a board member  of Özata Denizci, and he's inflating  Özata Denizci's shares. Look, Fatma  Betüshan Kaya is also buying those  shares, and they're using the same  method. And as Özata's shares inflate,  with all the money they earn from this,  the money they make from the shares,  like Fatma Betül Sayan and Kaya, they  go and sell it to a fund and get their  money. They leave. İskender Balcılı  was arrested. You remember. Barış  Pehlivan revealed it, both his  father-in-law and his relationship with  his father, and he's in prison now, but  when you look at it, they inflated  Özata Denizci's shares. Özdemir  Ataseven is also in prison, and you saw  the Tera connection here again. But  look, in the two points I've mentioned  and in what I'll say next, they all  know Ali Emre Ballı. They all have  very close relationships with Ali Emre  Ballı and Taat Çakmak. As you know,  Ali Emre Ballı was found dead in his  car, and it's alleged he committed  suicide. It's claimed to be a suicide.  But this is a death within a  multi-billion dollar corruption case,  and it's a suspicious death. That's why  I included Ali Emre Ballı in all of  them. We put him in the whole picture.  Because he has connections with all of  them. Ali Emre Ballı is connected to  Taat Çakmak, and it's known that Taat  Çakmak called him immediately after  his death. But when you look at it, you  see that Taat Çakmak, İskender Balcı , and all of them come together in this  picture. They are all connected. And  when we look at this picture, what do  we see in this context? A father, a son , a stock. Öz Atacilik, and there are  politicians, company owners, and death.  We see the same thing here. Look, when  we come to Tera, imagine that they are  all gathered there. Oğuz Tezmen is a  former high-ranking bureaucrat. From  the General Directorate of TY to the  Ministry of Transportation, to the  position of Deputy Undersecretary, he  is a name who has continuously served  in the state as a public servant, a  bureaucrat. Both father and son are  Emre Tezmen. He is the central figure  in this embezzlement scheme. The  central figure. If he spoke, if he  explained everything, we wouldn't need  to deal with these diagrams at all. He  knows everything well enough to reveal  the whole picture. If Emre Tezmen spoke , we wouldn't need to wait for lists  from the government. He could reveal  all the lists, showing who earned how  much. When we look at the Emre Tezmen  case, look, we explained to the BDDK ( Banking Regulation and Supervision  Agency) that he received bank  investment permits. Özata Denizcik is  just one of the dozens of stocks he  inflated. Gintürk and Green Türk are  also among the stocks he inflated. From  this, there are incredible  embezzlements, billions of liras,  through this system and its connection  to Ta Çakmak. We just talked about the  bribery relationships. Don't think that  Ta Çakman's benefit to Emre Tezmen was  limited to accumulating the money of  Türkiye Sigorta AŞ and Türkiye  Emeklilik Hayat Emeklilik AŞ. Don't  think it's just about transferring  resources here. He's also at one of the  centers that enables him to establish  all these relationships. And when you  look at it, there's Fatma Betü  Sayankaya and Ali Emre Ballı in Tera,  and a death. Because it's possible to  think that Ali Emre Ballı is also  involved in this scheme, especially due  to his connections with Tağa Çakmak.  And finally, there's Hayati Yazıcı.  We need to separate this. We can't  fully connect it here. Because here, we  know about the relationships between  the fathers, their bureaucratic  relationships. But here, Hayati  Yazıcı is the AKP deputy chairman.  Look, the names of several deputy  chairmen have come up in this scandal  so far: Hayati Yazıcı, Fatma  Betülsayan Kaya, and Nihat Ziyekçi.  Nihat Ziyekçi says he lost 250 million  TL. Hayati Yazıcı's name comes up  because of his son, Mustafa Yazıcı.  Mustafa Yazıcı is one of the owners  of Adil Asset Management. He's the name  behind the scenes. But the most  important thing is that he's Ali Emre  Ballı's partner. And when you look at  the system they established, there are  other partners as well. They even  published figures related to this.  Because you ask if there's a law for  trustees? Yes, there is. Because our  laws state that trustees are obligated  to manage the companies they are  appointed to with the prudence of a  businessman. So, when a trustee comes  there, they have to do their job well.  He says they have to work better than  the boss if necessary. But look, it  wasn't like that when a >> trustee was appointed to the  pro-government media. When a trustee is  appointed to critical media, we see  that they just shut down. We don't see  any prudence being shown at all. Why  did Halk TV shut down? I mean, it  didn't shut down, but why can't it  continue broadcasting? Why doesn't Halk  TV continue broadcasting, get  advertisements, perhaps pay its  employees 'salaries and try to do more?  No, that doesn't happen. Now I'll tell  you an example here. This happened  exactly this week. I wouldn't have been  aware of it if these developments  hadn't occurred. When I became aware, I  immediately tried to get this  information to you for the broadcast.  The subject is Tele1. Remember, what  happened to the public a year ago  happened to Tele1. Merdan Yanardağ was  arrested with a baseless espionage  investigation, and a trustee was  appointed to Tele1. When I heard what  happened in a year, I called Alp  Yanardağ, Merdan Yanardağ's son. Alp  was very distressed. When you hear why  he's distressed, I think you'll be  distressed too, watching from your  screens. Do you know why? Because of  this...Look, when the trustee took over  Tele 1 a year ago, Tele 1 was a  functioning channel. It had continuous  24-hour broadcasting, from morning news  to midnight bulletins. Around 126  employees. We don't know the exact  number because the people making the  programs change, etc., but that's what  I was told; it was a channel with  around 126 employees. It was paying  salaries every month. Salaries were  paid regularly every month, more or  less. And this channel actually had  debts, which is quite normal. I asked  Alpanardağ. How much debt did it have  a year ago? He said 30 million lira in  debt. This debt is payable. 25-30  million within the cycle. Think of it  this way: 25-30 million for this  channel, which is constantly operating.  It gets advertisements, it makes  expenses. It's not a huge debt. Let's  say you decided to sell the channel  that day, it's an amount that could  cover the debt. >> Now, why is Alpanardağ so worried?  Let's get to that point. Merdan  Yanardağ says this is actually quite  normal and legal. He's naming the  channel after his son. Why? Because his  son, being of a certain age, could own  the channel and build a future with it,  so he's naming it after his son. A  channel in Alp Yanardağ's name. But  after the trustee came, we say he  should have managed it like a prudent  businessman. He's managing these 126  people in such a way that T1 broadcasts  have practically stopped. >> Yes. >> You know, they're switching to recorded  broadcasts. They're >> not getting any advertising. Imagine  zero advertising. A job, zero  advertising. First, he's paying  salaries to 126 people, then he starts  laying off 30 people. Then he continues  to keep some of them employed. But  while he's keeping them employed and  paying their salaries, these people  aren't coming to work because they're  not his employees. The channel has to  pay salaries. On the other hand,  there's zero revenue on screen. It's  decreasing, decreasing, decreasing.  Paying salaries to some, paying  severance to others, but the channel  has no income at all. At the same time,  there are satellite expenses,  electricity bills, tax debts... >> I spoke with Alp Yanardağ. He said, " Right now, Barış abi..." I've known  Alp since childhood. Right now, as  Barış abi said, it's a channel that's  not functioning. By the way, it's no  longer broadcasting because it can't  pay its satellite revenue. When you  turn it on, you see something  completely black where Tele 1 used to  be. In other words, it's a channel on  the verge of liquidation. I'm not even  talking about selling it; it's at a  point where people will say, "I wish  they had sold it." Of course, I wish  they hadn't appointed a trustee at all.  I wish it hadn't been sold at all, but  if >> they had, remember, there would have  been talk of selling it for 28 million.  Maybe it would have been sold and its  debts paid off. That didn't happen  either. The channel's foundations were  practically destroyed with  sledgehammers. When you turn it on, you  see a black screen, and it's constantly  in debt, with zero income, now it's  non-operational, on the verge of  liquidation, and has reached the point  where Alpinardağ is being told, "You  now have 80 million in debt."  Alpinardağ says, "Barış abi, a year  ago, I owned a business that was  constantly functioning and could be  paid off." Merdan Yanardağ's son, a  trustee who should manage this like a  shrewd businessman, came and increased  the debt to 80 million. He says that in  the early days, since I appeared as the  owner of the channel, they always kept  me informed. Now, they don't even  answer my calls. They call me once a  month. That's the trustee's  responsibility. They give information,  say goodbye, >> and then they leave me with debt. >> Right now, I'm a person who has to live  with this debt for the rest of my life.  Since this channel is now dead, even if  I go and work as a waiter or a laborer  somewhere tomorrow, my salary will be  garnished for the rest of my life  because of these debts. I won't be able  to live a normal life. I probably won't  even earn 80 million in my lifetime,  even if I work. So, what I'm trying to  say is that this thing you call a  trustee can take different forms in  other places. Now, since Halk TV has  been appointed, maybe in a year we'll  have to talk about Halk TV here. But as  seen in the Tele1 example, appointing a  trustee is death for the viewer, death  for the channel, and it also creates a  death line that the owner, who founded  and created the channel with hope, will  carry for the rest of his life. Let's  also say this. By the way, >> Merdan abi has been living with this  debt on his shoulders for a year,  serving time in prison. You might ask,  who is this trustee? The trustee  appointed to Tele1 and the trustee  appointed to Halk TV are the same  person. So, the trustee who brought  Tele1 to this state, who should now be  managing it like a prudent businessman,  is now in charge of Halk TV. As you  know, Halk TV isn't actually  broadcasting at all. Just like you said , if a trustee is appointed to a  furniture factory, you'll continue  production. But for some reason, that  channel's broadcasts are also being  blocked. >> That channel's lifelines are being cut  off. Just as you were explaining all  this, Erdoğan's post-cabinet statement  came. I'm reading it verbatim: "We have  no problem with press freedom or  critical voices." Erdoğan says. Turkey  is one of the most advanced countries  in the world in terms of media  diversity. In Europe, our country ranks  among the top in terms of the number of  television channels. Hundreds of  television channels and thousands of  radio channels representing every  viewpoint broadcast freely in our  country. And we see this as a symbol of  Türkiye's social diversity. We welcome  different voices. I think we're living  in different countries than Erdoğan.  We've talked about Tele 1, Halk TV, and  journalists in prison. Murat Harel, one  of the most valuable assets of this  country, is in prison. We all know  about the closure of T24 and the dozens  of journalists we're mentioning all at  once. And Turkey is at the bottom of  the world in the press freedom index,  but according to Erdoğan, Turkey is  one of the best countries in the world  in terms of media diversity. Now I say  to everyone, grab your remote. While  Erdoğan is speaking, just press the  buttons on the remote and see how many  channels are broadcasting him, and pray  for diversity. Similarly, when an  opposition leader speaks, see where  their views are being broadcast. It's  very strange that these things can be  said in a single day, in a single  period, when trustees are appointed to  Halk TV and Tele 1. So, >> these statements unfortunately make us  feel like we're in a completely  different dystopian setting, like in a  Kafka novel. >> Now, I'm going to tell you about a very  important matter concerning Murat  Ağır. We're going to talk about a  very important, breaking news  development. The situation is perhaps  heading in a completely different  direction, and then we'll conclude. I  know we said an hour, but I think we're  a little over an hour. First, I  prepared an article today about Murat  Ağır. The subject of the article is  three separate pieces of evidence  showing Murat Ağırel's innocence. One  of them, I don't know if you remember,  is about two Germans, two German  citizens, and a Turk named Sinan  Çampar. They contacted Murat Ağırel  while he was pursuing the Gökçek case  and told him that they also had  something related to Sarıgül besides  the Gökçek case. Murat Ağırel  constantly asked them for documents. He  said that he needed documents to write  such a file. He said he could prove it  with documents. In the end, he became  suspicious of the document he received.  Because of his suspicion, he was taken  into custody before he could write the  file, based on their complaint. Now,  the other day, while I was on Sözcü  TV, Saygı Öztürk showed a document.  This is our first topic. That document,  the one on the left, is the part that  made Murat Ağırel suspicious of the  document that German citizens sent him.  Do you know what it is? Sinan  Çampınar said this: "We sent 100  million euros to the Sarıgül family.  Here you go, Murat. Here's the receipt. " When Murat said, as he told them, " I'll ask the other side about this,"  this receipt on the left appeared. A  Denizbank receipt. Because Sarıgül's  lawyer told Murat, and Sarıgül's  lawyer also says it, and Murat himself  says it, "No, it wasn't 100 million  euros. Sarıgül himself also says it  in a social media statement. They sent  euros. We sent those euros back. Here's  the receipt." So when Saygı Öztürk  showed this receipt on air, I thought,  "This is very interesting. This is  important. Frankly, as a journalist, if  I saw this receipt, I would also have  suspicions." So Murat was right to be  suspicious. The story he told wasn't  baseless. Secondly, something even  stranger happened. There's a journalist  colleague of ours, Ercan Öztürk,  who's on the media radar, and he's very  experienced. More experienced than us.  In fact, I worked as a reporter with >> Ercan for years. >> Then Ercan Öztürk did something  interesting. He went to check the  address of the company founded by Murat  Ağırel, two German citizens, and  Sinan Çampınar, who are complainants  in this case. He went to an address in  Bakırköy, SKM Global Energy, and what  did he see? This company turned out to  be a shell company. You know how it's  become fashionable lately to not even  keep an office, not even an address?  For example, this is an address. We  have a building right now. You don't  keep an address. You rent an address to  show as an address. A virtual office,  and you pay 1000 L, 2000 L, 3000 L,  5000 L a month. Someone there receives  your mail on your behalf. Do you know  that the phone turned up in a place  like this? I mean, the big energy  company, the company that's supposedly  going to build Tesla factories in  Erzincan, the company that sent 100  million euros, >> Ercan Öztürk found it–you'll see  the photo on the right. The company  kept an address in a virtual office.  And do you know what's funny? Ercan  Öztürk wrote about it in the news.  Because they didn't even pay the rent  for the virtual office, they were  kicked out and thrown out for  2,000-3,000 lira. This is actually one  of the things that proves my doubts  about how serious and real the other  side was, as Murat Alel said. Thirdly,  I called Murat Alel's lawyer. I asked  if they had appealed the arrest over  the weekend? Olsan Aslan said yes. Can  I have the petition? "He said. When I  read the appeal, I saw this: Murat  Ağırel has given the court recordings  of all his meetings with these German  citizens and Sinan Çampınar, both  phone recordings and video recordings. >> But let me explain why he obtained  these recordings. There is a statement  from a lawyer that the people on the  other side were recording him. And  because these people were already  involved in >> money laundering activities, he  suspected them of setting a trap and  tried to record every step cautiously. >> I read the transcript of those  recordings because the transcript is in  the file. >> In the transcript, you can see that  Murat Ağırel, while pursuing the  Gökçek case, was actually drawn into  the Sarıgül issue. And there's  something there, I'm quoting from the  transcript, he says in his meeting, you  know, Murat Ağırel is accused of  giving information to Sarıgül, and  someone always says in his meeting,' I  will ask the other side, 'he >> always says >> this in these conversations. >> On the other hand, Sinan Çampınar  says,' I think, 'from a female lawyer ..." They are suspicious. So, this  woman also cultivated something for the  yellow roses. I was already suspicious  of this. This woman, while you were in  Germany, while Murat Ağıral was  telling you about a few incidents, you  were on a street, she held a camera to  the ground and recorded you. So, the  other side's suspicion wasn't Murat  Ağıral, but this woman, that a lawyer  recorded Murat Ağıral and informed  the yellow roses. Somehow, the incident  later blew up in Murat Ağıral's face.  On the other hand, you know how there's  a kind of character assassination  against Murat Ağıral lately? The  other side keeps saying, "Make the news , make the news, even without evidence. " Murat Ağıral says he won't make  news without evidence. And when these  discussions arose, these discussions in  Türkiye arose, even before he was  detained, there's a recording of this.  Murat openly says, insisting, "Did you  make any offer to me regarding this  news, or any financial expectation, or  any offer related to this news?"  Because when such rumors are voiced by  some politicians, >> of course, no. They say, "Why are we  even talking about this, Mr. Murat?"  The recordings are already there, and  I'm saying this because I asked Murat  Öen's lawyer if I could publish them.  He said publishing them might cause  legal problems. Actually, if Türkiye  had a normal legal system, there would  be no problem publishing them. Because  there are Supreme Court rulings. You  can take anything from the file and  make it into news. It has news value  once it's in the file. But secondly,  you can always publish these kinds of  recordings to prove someone's guilt or  innocence. >> For example, if I saw a case of  violence against a woman, I could film  it and publish it. The woman could also  present it to the court. >> Of course, it's >> a crime committed against her. There  are Supreme Court rulings, but we're  not in a normal legal system. Mr.  Barış said, "If you want, you can  publish the petition itself, of course,  but I'm not sure about publishing these  images or these conversations." So I'm  making a call from here. Allow us to  publish them. Allow us to publish them.  Allow us. Let everyone hear who Murat  Ağırel spoke to and what he said.  What did he say? Everything is already  recorded. >> What about the conversation with the  complainant? >> What did he say? Let it be heard, let  it be listened to. Let's condemn him  accordingly, criticize him, or say, " Maybe it wasn't like that," let's see.  But I think...This will be another call  from here, but let's >> especially emphasize this again. For  example, Murat Aril is under accusation . While there is not a single piece of  evidence related to the accusation,  there are so many pieces of evidence  proving his innocence, his lack of  guilt—correspondence, video  recordings, audio recordings—that  prove his innocence, yet he continues  to serve his sentence. >> In Türkiye, unfortunately, you have to  prove your innocence. >> That's exactly what he did. >> Now, as I was coming to this broadcast,  I received a critical phone call. Mr.  Barış, uh, there was an important  detention. In the Sarıgül case, that  is, the Sarıgül case in which Murat  Ağırel was also arrested, and it was  said that this would change the  complexion of the case. And indeed, our  colleague Büşra Cebeci from Gazete  Pencere reported this news. You will  say, who was detained? Serkan Korkutata  was detained. In the evening, Büşra  Cebeci published the news from Gazete  Pencere. Serkan Korkut You may not know  Atay. Let me repeat. Serkan Korkutata,  who was detained in the Sarıgül  investigation, is the Deputy Chairman  of the AKP Ankara Provincial Branch.  That's one of his characteristics. So,  the person detained in the Sarıgül  investigation is currently an AKP  executive. Let's move on to the second  detail. A very important >> name is Serkan Korkutata; beyond being  the Deputy Chairman of the AKP Ankara  Provincial Branch, you know his  writings, especially those of Murat  Ağırel, from years ago. He's known  for the very large, systematic tenders  he received from the Ankara  Metropolitan Municipality, as reported  repeatedly in newspapers like Bir Gün  and Cumhuriyet about the Gökçek  family. And the critical media  constantly publishes news questioning  the tenders Serkan Korkutata received  from the Ankara Metropolitan  Municipality. Murat Ağırel and others  like him know him not only as the  Deputy Chairman of the AKP Ankara  Provincial Branch but also as a  politician very close to the Gökçek  family. Then I sat down and thought  about what I meant by the phone call I  received after reading this news. I  think I was saying something like this  in the article I wrote today: Murat  Ağırel, while chasing the Gökçek  case, fell into the Sarıgül case. You  know how there are interconnected  vessels in physics? It's like this...It  seems like two separate investigations  are merging through Serkan Korkutata.  So I want to ask this: why is Murat  Öğren in prison then? He's going to >> expose the Gökçek criminal  organization, so I hope that Murat  Öğren and Serkan Korkutata, who have  been working together for years, won't  be side-by-side as defendants. Murat  Öğren will probably say, "Let him get  out, I'll stay as a defendant." That's  the kind of situation he's living in.  His >> book, the spiral book, etc. >> Before I leave, if you have nothing  else to say, I'll finish. >> Before I leave, let's give Murat  Öğren's mailing address once more.  Let's remind our viewers of the mailing  address at Kandıra Prison. Our viewers  may not have seen it at the beginning.  Kocaeli No. 2 F-type prison, B2, Room 4 , Room 61, PTT Prison Branch. When you  write this in the address section of  your letter, the letters you write  inside go to Murat Öğren. Remember,  your letters are being read. Because  people ask me this a lot. Don't write  as if they're not being read. It's  assumed that a third party is reading  them. It's being read. It's stamped " read" and then published. We mentioned  this at the beginning of the broadcast.  Our dear Aunt Şule is absent because  she experienced the joy of becoming an  aunt at the last minute. Barış hasn't  been able to go for a while due to  these events. He's absent because he  hasn't seen his daughter. Timur and I  tried to manage this, but I hope you  had a very fulfilling time. We tried to  give a lot of news, to cram a lot of  news into this short time. Thank you.  Thank you. >> Good evening. Our >> main theme was fathers and sons. Since  we talked about Murat, since we talked  about fathers and sons, let's end with  Turgenev's fathers and sons again.  Personality, sir, that's the most  important thing. A person's personality  should be as solid as a rock. Because  everything is built upon it. We know  that our friend built his journalism  upon a rock-solid personality. We are  witnesses, and I'm sure everyone will  see it. Thank you very much. Good  evening from them. Let's talk. Even if >> we are banned from screens, even if we  are removed from newspapers, even if we  are removed from social media, even if  we use smoke signals, even if we use  wall newspapers, we will continue to  tell society something. If we leave the  children alone, we will plunge the  future of this country into darkness.  Not the youth, not the journalists, not  the children...
